is a resume builder. You upload an old resume, talk through your history out loud, or fill in a form — and you get a typeset PDF that an applicant tracking system can actually read.

Most resumes are rejected by software before a person sees them, and most resume tools do not tell you that. A file can look immaculate on screen and still come apart when a parser reads it: two-column layouts that interleave, headings that extract one character at a time, bullet markers that push every bullet after every employer.

The AI restructures and rephrases what you give it. It is forbidden from inventing employers, job titles, dates, degrees or credentials — a hard constraint with no exceptions. Where it proposes a number it cannot verify, it marks it as an unconfirmed estimate, highlights it, and lists every one of them before you download. When it does not know something, it asks you rather than filling the gap.

Your resume is sent only to providers contractually bound not to retain or train on it, pinned in configuration — and the app refuses to start in production if that configuration is missing. The details are in the
